channel.title: Brisbane s calendar Light up Brisbane
channel.description: This calendar includes scheduled lights ups of Council assets including Story Bridge, Reddacliff Place sculptures, Victoria Bridge, Brisbane City Hall, King George Square, William Jolly Bridge and Tropical Dome at Brisbane Botanic Gardens Mt Coot-tha.

item.title: War Widows Day Queensland 2026
item.description:
Monday, 19 October 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit Blue to support War Widows Day Queensland 2026

The annual War Widows Day, officially acknowledged by the Queensland Government in 2022, aims to increase awareness about the array of resources and support accessible to war widows and widowers. Additionally, it stands as a poignant reminder of the profound loss experienced by the families and friends of those who have served Australia.

This Light Up is organised by: Australian War Widows Queensland

Light up asset: Reddacliff Place, Brisbane City
Venue address: Reddacliff Place, 266 George Street, Brisbane City
Venue type: General Council venue, Light up asset

item.title: Sexual Violence Awareness Month
item.description:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit Teal to support Sexual Violence Awareness Month

October is Sexual Violence Awareness Month in Queensland.
It is a month where sexual assault organisations around the state give attention to engagement in the community - providing avenues for the community to learn about this issue and feel able to support stands against this violence.

This Light Up is organised by: Zig Zag Young Women's Resource Centre

item.title: Dysautonomia Awareness Month
item.description:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Teal to support Dysautonomia Awareness Month

Dysautonomia Awareness Month raises awareness and aims to empower people with the condition and their families. Dysautonomia is an umbrella term used to describe several different medical conditions that cause a malfunction of the Autonomic Nervous System. Dysautonomia Australia - purpose is to raise awareness for invisible illnesses that come under the banner of dysautonomia

This Light Up is organised by: Dysautonomia Australia

item.title: International Stuttering Awareness Day
item.description:
Thursday, 22 October 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Sea Green to support International Stuttering Awareness Day

STUTTA, trading as the Australian Stuttering Association, exists to encourage and empower people who stutter to embrace their individual journeys. Our vision is a world in which people who stutter are given the space, time, and opportunity to speak. To learn more about STUTTA and resources for stuttering, visit stutta.org.
International Stuttering Awareness Day is intended to raise awareness about stuttering which affects 1% to 5% of the population, equating to 28k to 140k in Brisbane and 278k to 1.39M within Australia

This Light Up is organised by: STUTTA

item.description:

City Hall will be lit Gold to celebrate the Lord Mayor's Multicultural Business Awards

item.title: Water Night
item.description:
Thursday, 22 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Blue to support Water Night

Water Night is a national water literacy campaign held during National Water Week, inviting Australians to turn off their taps for five hours on Thursday 22 October 2026 and notice the role water plays in their everyday routines. The campaign aims to make water more visible in daily life, build awareness of water efficiency and inspire practical, lasting habits at home, school and in the community.

This Light Up is organised by: The Water Conservancy

item.title: Eve of Melt Festival River Pride Parade and Brisbane Pride Festival
item.description:
Friday, 23 October 2026

Reddacliff Place sculptures will be lit all colours to celebrate the Eve of Melt Festival River Pride Parade and Brisbane Pride Festival

River Pride Parade will set sail and help make Brisbane River/Maiwar sparkle with pride in the dazzling rainbow flotilla. Celebrating all our LGBTQIA+ communities and allies in true Brisbane style… by boat! From yachts to jetskis, join the colourful flotilla cruising from West End to Brisbane Powerhouse as part of the MELT Festival.
MELT Festival is an 'open access' festival of Queer arts held annually in central Brisbane. The Event is a collaboration between Brisbane Powerhouse, local artists and performance spaces and will be held across a range of Brisbane's clubs, pubs, galleries, theatres, and non-traditional performance spaces from 21 Oct - 8 Nov 2026

This Light Up is organised by: Brisbane Economic Development Agency and Brisbane Pride Festival Inc

Light up asset: Reddacliff Place, Brisbane City
Venue address: Reddacliff Place, 266 George Street, Brisbane City
Venue type: General Council venue, Light up asset

Victoria Bridge will be lit Rainbow to celebrate the Eve of Melt Festival River Pride Parade and Brisbane Pride Festival
River Pride Parade will set sail and help make Brisbane River/Maiwar sparkle with pride in the dazzling rainbow flotilla. MELT Festival is an 'open access' festival of Queer arts held annually in central Brisbane. item.title: CEO Cookout
item.description:
Tuesday, 27 October 2026

Kangaroo Point Bridge will be lit Yellow to support CEO Cookout

We're helping to feed people in need! We're taking part in OzHarvest's CEO CookOff this October to cook meals and raise crucial funds to feed people in need in our local communities. With the cost of living increasing, the demand for food relief in Australia is at an all-time high as people struggle to make ends meet. We're teaming up with Australia's most talented chefs, and other CEOs and leaders to reduce food waste and make a difference to Australia’s most vulnerable as every $1 donated to OzHarvest means they can deliver 2 meals to those in need. Every donation counts, so please sponsor our team to cook, connect and create change to help those doing it tough

This Light Up is organised by: Oz Harvest

item.description:
Thursday, 29 October 2026

City Hall will be lit Green to celebrate the Canegrowers Centenary Celebrations

In 2026, CANEGROWERS celebrates 100 years of representing Queensland's sugarcane farming families and advocating for one of the State's most important agricultural industries. The milestone recognises the contribution of generations of growers and regional communities. Sugarcane's significance is reflected on the Queensland Coat of Arms, and today the industry continues to celebrate the more than 23,000 jobs and contribute billions of dollars through sugar, renewable energy, biofuels and exports.

This Light Up is organised by: CANEGROWERS

item.title: UQ Medical School 90th Anniversary
item.description:
Saturday, 31 October 2026

Victoria Bridge will be lit Purple to celebrate the UQ Medical School 90th Anniversary

The University of Queensland's Medical School is one of Australia's most respected and internationally recognised medical schools, and is celebrating its 90th Anniversary in 2026. We provide high-quality teaching and practical training through world-class programs in medicine, mental health and skin cancer. We ensure all graduates are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to fulfil their ethical and professional responsibilities, face medical challenges, and advance health and well-being through life-long education and research. The Medical School is also research-orientated and we continue to address the world's evolving health priorities by driving innovative research that advances knowledge, practices and discoveries that improve the lives of patients.

This Light Up is organised by: University of Queensland Medical School
